name: Household store for dated schedules and single facts (in-house tool plugin)
description: A small household database that both parents' agents and the timed jobs read and update: dated schedules (filter every 90 days, last oil change) and single facts a job needs. It is the shared back end of the upkeep rows in the renewals look-ahead (F063) and of the other dated features; handbook-style knowledge lives in the vault (F043) and each parent's own notes in memory (F041).
example: Tony texts: 'did the furnace filter today'. Six weeks later Jordan asks 'when is the furnace filter due?' and gets the same date Tony's agent would give.
how: In-house defineToolPlugin over node:sqlite with schedule_get/upsert/mark_done and fact_get/set; allowlisted on both mains and in tools.sandbox.tools; secret check inside execute or via definePluginEntry.
caveats: The first version has only the schedule and fact tools. Features that keep their own rows here (the sick-day log in CRT-10, open requests in G009's relay step, the notification counters in G001, the change journal in G006) add their own table and tool when they are built.

Not every later table is meant for both parents: the change journal (G006) keeps each parent's rows in this store, among them a copy of the text of each note that parent saved to memory, and its read tool has to return only the asker's rows. That filter is G006's own code and is tested there; the schedule and fact tools apply no per-person filter.
corrections: The 9 Oct verifier note says the secret-rejecting before_tool_call hook can live in the same plugin as the defineToolPlugin store. docs/plugins/tool-plugins.md:11 says defineToolPlugin adds tools only, and :233 points to definePluginEntry when tools are combined with hooks.

The catalog chooses defineToolPlugin for the store but still names its tools home-store__schedule_* in the automations. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:242 gives that server__tool form to MCP servers only; a plugin's tools carry the names it declares, so job tool lists must use those.
unverified: node:sqlite is labelled release candidate on nodejs.org; no long-run test of it inside the gateway process was done.
safety: Both parents' agents and the timed jobs read and write the same schedule and fact rows, so anything stored through those tools is shared between the two adults by design; something meant for one parent belongs in that parent's own memory (F041). 'Shared by design' covers those tools and not every table in the file: the change journal (G006) plans a table here that holds each parent's own rows, including a copy of saved memory notes, and it has to be kept to its owner inside that card's read tool. The plugin refuses values that look like secrets. Like a memory note, a stored fact is read back later by the other parent's agent and by jobs, so it is a place where an injected instruction could persist: facts should stay short and typed (a date, an interval, a short label), not free text lifted from a page or a document.

name: Durable per-person memory: 'remember this' is saved to that parent's own notes and found again, by keyword first and by meaning as a later step
description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent writes the fact to its notes and finds it again in later chats; where those notes live is an open decision that settles whether a saved note survives the next deploy and whether it is in view at the start of a chat or found only when Happy searches. Notes are found by their words at first; a later, optional step adds search by meaning for text notes, with the indexing done on the Mac mini.
example: Jordan texts: 'Remember that piano moved to Thursdays at 4.' A week later she asks 'which day is piano?' and gets Thursday at 4. After the later step, 'what was the kid's nut thing again?' finds the note that says 'tree-nut allergy', although none of the words match.
how: Notes (F041): allow write and edit on each parent's agent, with a read-write workspace and apply_patch denied by name; an in-house before_tool_call hook limits write paths, by default to memory/*.md (MEMORY.md and USER.md stay with the F042 generator unless a live test shows a chat write does not stop them loading); memory_search and memory_get with keyword-only search set explicitly (`memory.search.provider: "none"`; unset, the documented default is OpenAI embeddings); the bundled session-memory hook. Later step (F046): install the official llama.cpp provider plugin, run its embedding-only setup, set the provider to `local` with `fallback: "none"` and re-index; the same search also covers the family handbook (F043). Further option: Active Memory, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
caveats: Where chat-saved notes live is undecided: as read in the installed docs and code and not tried on a live turn, a chat write to MEMORY.md or USER.md from a sender who is not the command owner (today every turn of Jordan's), after web content in the same turn, or after the family-facts generator (F042) has re-rendered the file marks the whole file untrusted, and an untrusted file no longer loads at the start of a chat, the generated family facts in it included.

Keeping saved notes in memory/*.md avoids that at a cost: only today's and yesterday's dated notes load at a fresh start and older ones are found only when the agent searches, so until the choice is made and tested for both parents a saved note is not guaranteed to come back.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper, so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.

Refusing a memory write in a turn that carried web or research results is not something the platform does for a file write: no taint flag that a hook can read was found, so the in-house hook has to track web tool calls itself, and this is untested.
Notes belong to one parent; something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Until the later step is done a saved note is found by its words and not by its meaning, and whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting has not been tested.

Search by meaning covers text only, because on this version photo and audio indexing works only with Google's cloud embedding model, and how much it would improve on keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a measured figure.
If the embedding server on the Mac mini fails, search drops back to keyword matching without telling the parent; the reason shows only in a debug field.
corrections: The catalog relies on `sessions_search` with visibility `agent` to find pre-reset conversations. docs/gateway/config-tools/sessions-and-subagents.md:58 says a sandboxed session stays limited to sessions it spawned while agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility is 'spawned' (the default); the mains run with sandbox mode all, so that key must change as well. docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md:372 adds that tools.sessions.visibility is gateway-wide, not per agent.

The catalog ties this to M2 (local models). docs/plugins/llama-cpp.md:123 documents an embedding-only setup that adds no chat model, so the text leg does not depend on M2 and can be done on the installed stack.

The 9 Oct reason for dropping photo search is that no local multimodal embedder exists. Google's EmbeddingGemma page now describes EmbeddingGemma 2 as multimodal and local; the actual block is that OpenClaw 2026.9.7 only indexes images with gemini-embedding-2 (docs/reference/memory-config.md:495).
unverified: Whether visibility 'self' already reaches the same chat's pre-reset history (the docs define self as the current session key) was not tested.

No taint flag that a plugin hook can read was found in the hook docs opened, although OpenClaw's memory design does mark a turn as tainted after web content (memory-architecture.md:117); so 'refuse writes after web results' means the hook tracking web tool calls itself. Untested.

How a direct agent write to a memory file is classified was read in the installed code, not seen on a live turn: the write is recorded as agent-written only in a command owner's turn with no web content, and only if the file has not changed since its last recorded write; otherwise the whole file is recorded as untrusted (dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496, dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). MEMORY.md and USER.md load at the start of a chat only while their record counts as eligible (memory-architecture.md:215). Check on a live turn for each parent.
Whether a note saved in one of Jordan's turns (she is not the command owner) comes back from memory_search like any other note, or is shown to the model with an untrusted label, was not tested.
Whether the F042 generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked; the generator was not opened.

Whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting was not tested: the engine page lists Chinese support through trigram tokenization (memory-builtin.md:23), the config reference gives `unicode61` as the default tokenizer with `trigram` as the alternative (reference/memory-config.md:625), and the search guide's fix for Chinese text that is not found is a forced re-index (memory-search.md:226). F042's own example has Jordan writing to Happy in Chinese, so the live test should include one such note.

How an untrusted label is cleared once it is set was not found: in the code read, the label recorded for a file is returned without comparing it with the file's current contents (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:49), so a re-render by the generator may not bring a file back into the start of a chat.
Whether the managed llama.cpp server in 2026.9.7 can load EmbeddingGemma 2 was not checked.
The gain over keyword search for a few hundred family notes is a judgement, not a sourced figure.
Whether search by meaning finds a note saved in Chinese from a question asked in English, or the reverse, was not tested; it depends on the embedding model chosen.
safety: Notes stay in each parent's own agent; shared agents such as research hold none. The one planned copy outside it comes with the change journal (G006): that card keeps the text of each saved note in its table in the household store (F031), to be returned only to the note's owner by the journal's own read tool, and correcting or deleting a note has to delete that row too. A fail-closed before_tool_call hook limits writes to the memory files, and apply_patch is denied by name. A saved note is where an injected instruction could persist; the weekly review (G006) shows what was saved. The later step embeds on the Mac mini with no cloud fallback and adds no tool or send path.

name: Family facts, standing preferences and reply language rendered into each parent's agent from family.json5
description: Both parents' agents start every one-to-one chat already knowing the kids' school, routines and activities and each adult's standing preferences, including the language to reply in. On request Happy also turns a school note into a short Chinese text a parent can forward to a grandparent.
example: Jordan writes to Happy in Chinese and is answered in Chinese; Tony texts 'put this school note in Chinese for grandma' and gets three short lines to forward.
how: One generator, one file. From family.json5 the generator renders each adult's directives into USER.md (4,000-character cap), the per-person reply-language line among them (G011), and the kid and routine facts into MEMORY.md with trigger comments (F042); nothing is rendered into shared agents. A scheduled job does not infer a reply language from the chat and does not load MEMORY.md, so the language, and any family fact a job needs, is written into the job message or AGENTS.md. The two rendered files stay generator-only: what a parent asks Happy to remember in chat is saved elsewhere (F041). The grandparent version is a prompt-only request on the parent's own agent: no new tool and no send path, and the parent forwards the text.
caveats: USER.md has a 4,000-character cap that all standing preferences share, so the list has to stay short.

Rendered facts change only when the family file is edited and redeployed, and a chat edit to a generated file is expected to be lost on the next deploy; things a parent says in chat go through the memory write path (F041).

The kid and routine facts sit in MEMORY.md, which loads at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat only: scheduled jobs, the group chat and hand-offs to a helper do not get it (user-model.md:376), so a brief that needs a routine carries it in AGENTS.md or in its job message.

Happy should not write to the two rendered files from chat. OpenClaw records where each memory file's last write came from, and a write in a turn from a sender who is not the command owner (Jordan today), a write after web content, or a second chat write after the generator has re-rendered the file marks the whole file untrusted, after which it is no longer loaded at the start of a chat (memory-architecture.md:112 and :217; dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496; dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). Read, not tried on a live turn; the write hook in F041 is where this is enforced.

On supported iPhones Messages can already translate a conversation automatically and on device, so plain back-and-forth with a grandparent may need nothing from Happy; whether that covers Chinese on this family's phones is not confirmed.
Happy's distinct part on the language side is the shortened Chinese version of a school note, and its translation quality for school notices was not evaluated.

A per-language voice switch is documented only for the bundled Microsoft speech provider, which is an online service, so it does not help the offline say path, and whether the default say voice pronounces Chinese was not tested.
The generator script and the family registry were not opened in this review.
corrections: A 9 Oct verifier note says there is no per-language voice switch. tts/output.md:56 documents one for the bundled Microsoft provider, which is an online service; it does not help the offline say path.
unverified: The generator script and the family registry live in happy-config and were not opened in this run.
That a chat edit to a generated file is lost on the next deploy is a property of Tony's generator, not something an opened source states.
Translation quality into Chinese by gpt-6-sol for school notices was not evaluated.
Which iPhone models and languages Apple's Live Translation covers for this family was not confirmed; the Apple page defers to an availability list.
Whether the macOS say default voice pronounces Chinese text was not tested.

Whether a scheduled run loads USER.md was not tried on a live job: the installed code lists it among the files a scheduled run gets and leaves MEMORY.md out (dist/workspace-DmDIneFk.mjs:742), while the scheduler guide only says a job does not infer a reply language (cron-jobs/delivery.md:140).
safety: The rendered files hold the children's school and routines, so they go only into the two parents' own agents and never into shared agents such as research, the group agent or the mail readers. No tool and no send path are added; a translated note leaves the family only when a parent forwards it.

name: Household knowledge vault: shared family handbook, including the home systems and service-provider registry
description: One shared family handbook that both parents' agents can search: people, home systems, providers, policy and warranty summaries, sitter notes. Dates that need a reminder live in the renewals table (F063), not here. A photo of an appliance's data plate, sent once, fills in the home-systems page, so a later 'what filter does the furnace take?' or 'who fixed the boiler?' gets the stored answer.
example: Tony sends a photo of the furnace data plate and texts 'save this'. A month later Jordan asks: 'What filter does the furnace take?'
how: Step 1 (F043): a shared Markdown folder added to each main's `memory.search.extraPaths`, searched with keyword-only memory search (`memory.search.provider: "none"`, set explicitly as in F041). Step 2: enable the bundled memory-wiki plugin with `vaultMode` left at `isolated` (the default), `vault.scope` global and its own vault directory; `wiki_search`, `wiki_get`, `wiki_apply` and `wiki_lint` on the two mains only. Registry (F034): with inbound attachments on, the vision model reads the data plate and the agent saves a wiki synthesis page with `wiki_apply`, or a fact in the household store; manuals given as a link go through the research agent. With only step 1 in place, the operator types the plate details into the folder by hand.
caveats: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart.
That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested.
Saving a data plate as a wiki page needs step 2; with only the shared folder the operator types the details in by hand.
Data-plate photos go to the cloud vision model, which is the attachments decision recorded under F002, and image input on the family's custom provider ids was not re-checked.
The vault is shared by design, so both parents' agents search and edit the same pages.

Other entries file into it: the renewals look-ahead keeps a policy's one-line summary page here, and a pet's vet contact and food reorder link would sit in the provider registry, with nothing ordered.
unverified: The two installed pages disagree on whether enabling memory-wiki needs a gateway restart (docs/plugins/memory-wiki.md:26 says it applies to a running gateway, docs/cli/wiki.md:15 shows a restart).

That memory_search in a sandboxed main can read a shared folder outside its workspace was not tested. The installed code labels files indexed from outside an agent's workspace as untrusted origin (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:32); whether that changes how handbook pages come back from search was not tested either.
That gpt-6-sol accepts images on Tony's custom provider ids was not checked in this run.
The memory-wiki route needs that bundled plugin enabled (F043 step 2); with only the shared Markdown folder, the operator types the plate details in by hand.
safety: Vault pages are private family data and belong on the two parents' own agents, which have no browse tool; the research agent that reads manuals holds none of it. The vault is one for the whole gateway. OpenClaw's page says to give each agent its own vault when agents must not share wiki pages (memory-wiki.md:59), and in that mode every agent gets a separate vault, so the two parents could not share one; with the shared vault the other agents are kept out by tool policy alone: the wiki tools go to the two mains only, and because the pages can also be reached through ordinary memory search where the memory engine supports it (memory-wiki.md:298), memory search stays off on the shared agents and the mail readers. Leave the plugin in its default `isolated` mode: as read on the same page (line 467) and not tried, bridge mode checks which agent owns an imported memory note only for per-agent vaults, so on the shared vault it could compile each parent's own notes (F041) into the handbook. A data-plate photo is untrusted content read by an agent with memory; that agent has no browser or fetch tool, and the ways out the roadmap lists for it are a text to its owner (or, once family delivery exists, the family) and the task text it hands to the research helper, which the roadmap names as the one remaining leak path. Once step 2 lets an agent write pages, the handbook is also a place where an instruction hidden in a photo, a document or a research result could persist, and because the vault is shared the other parent's agent reads it back too; the agent is told to save a page only when a parent asks (an instruction, not an enforced limit), and the weekly review (G006) as written today lists memory-file saves and in-house tool writes but not `wiki_apply` pages, so vault saves need a row there when step 2 is built.

name: Teach Happy a routine (operator-reviewed skills), with a parent-run practice quiz as the first skill
description: A parent describes once how the family does something (party plan, ski-trip packing, school-form explainer); Tony turns it into a named skill, and after the next deploy Happy can load it when a later request fits the skill's one-line description. The first skill is a practice quiz that a parent runs from a study-guide photo, a pasted spelling list or a request for math facts: ten questions, one at a time, hint first, a running score and the answer key at the end.
example: 'Happy, learn our ski-trip packing routine: ask how many nights and who is coming, then list by person, and always include the kids' helmets.' Or Jordan sends a photo of the science study guide and texts: 'quiz us on this, 10 questions, one at a time.'
how:
Pipeline (AUT-06): Happy answers with the drafted procedure as plain text; Tony turns it into `skills//SKILL.md` in happy-config, reviews it, and happy-deploy copies it into that agent's workspace `skills/` folder. The model loads a skill by reading its SKILL.md, so `

-main` needs `read` in `tools.alsoAllow` and the sandbox tool allowlist; `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent. A routine of a few lines can live in AGENTS.md instead. Quiz (MKT-02): one such skill fixes the format (one question per message, one hint before revealing, a running score, the answer key at the end, no web lookups); a photo needs attachment intake (F002) and is read by the reply model's own vision; an optional one-shot reminder offers a re-quiz the night before.
depends_on: a skills step in happy-deploy and gen-family
automatic self-learning switched off in config (`skills.workshop.autonomous.mode: "off"`)
decision: who may request a new skill

`read` allowed on

-main in tools.alsoAllow and the sandbox tool allowlist (group:fs is denied today; per-person memory, F041, adds `write` and `edit` only, so `read` is a grant of its own)
F041's write-path hook refusing any write under skills/, proven with a test write (needed once F041 gives the same agent a read-write workspace)
F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments switched on, for the quiz's photo route only

F007 automations tool on

-main, only for the optional re-quiz reminder
F003 voice over iMessage, its local spoken replies, only for reading spelling words aloud
caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool, and the documented exception would publish with no pending draft and so skip Tony's review, which is one more reason to keep that tool off every family agent.
A skill is know-how: it cannot add tools or accounts, so 'learn to order the groceries' still ends at a list.

A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions, so one written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection: author only from the parent's own words, and install no marketplace skills (an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026).

Turnaround is 'when Tony next deploys', and Happy does not run a skill every time: the prompt lists only each skill's name and one-line description, so that line has to be precise, and calling the skill by name (`/skill <name>`) is the sure route where that command is accepted from the sender.

The quiz is parent-run only: the kids are not users, the parent holds the phone and sends the answers, and a version a child uses alone waits for the kids agent (F072) and never uses a cloud model or cloud speech.

The ChatGPT or Gemini app on a parent's phone already makes a quiz from uploaded material, with hints and an end summary; Happy's only edge is that it lives in the same thread and can schedule the re-quiz.
Models write wrong answer keys, especially for arithmetic and for facts the sheet does not state, so tell it to quiz only from what is on the page and spot-check.

A text quiz shows spelling words on screen, so spelling practice needs the words read aloud with the local voice (F003), whose quality for spelling words is untried, and the running score lives in the conversation and is gone after the daily session reset.

Once per-person memory (F041) gives a parent's agent `write` and `edit` on a read-write workspace, the workspace skills folder sits inside what the agent can write: for that mode the docs describe a read-only copy only for bundled, managed and plugin skills (workspace-access.md:91) and do not say the workspace skills folder is protected. 'No model-written file reaches a skills folder' then rests on F041's in-house path hook, so that hook's proof must include a refused write to skills/.
safety: Operator review is the gate: `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent, a skill cannot widen tool policy, and no model-written file is meant to reach a skills folder. Once per-person memory (F041) lets the same agent write files in its workspace, that last point rests on F041's write-path hook and has to be proven with a refused write to skills/. The quiz is the riskier part: a photographed school worksheet is untrusted content, is not screened by the PDF privacy gate in F002, and goes to the cloud vision model under store:false. No child's account talks to a cloud model.
unverified: Whether a user-invocable skill command typed by an allowlisted non-owner iMessage sender is accepted on 2026.9.7.
That skill sync into the sandbox works with `workspaceAccess: "none"` (the docs say sandboxed runs read materialized copies).

That a `read`-only grant on a sandboxed

-main reaches the mirrored skills and nothing private; check at build time.
Whether an iMessage owner turn is ever given library-authoring authority on this configuration. If it is, an allowlisted `skill_workshop` could publish a skill with no review.
Whether a spoken reply arrives as a playable voice message or as a file in iMessage Basic mode.
The quality of the macOS say voice for spelling words was not tried.

name: Read-only Gmail for each parent through gog's MCP server (a token, no password): a 07:00 digest of the whole inbox and 'did I get an email about X?'
description: Each parent approves read-only access to their own Gmail once, on Google's consent screen; Google issues a token that stays on the Mac mini, and Happy never holds a password. One locked-down mail agent per adult uses that token through gog's MCP server. In wave A, at 07:00 the agent texts about ten lines on mail that needs a reply, has a deadline or involves money (from January to April a Saturday text adds which expected tax forms have had an arrival email), with the school lines first (F051). The second half, where a parent asks 'did the dentist confirm?' and gets the sender, the date and the gist, does not fit in wave A beside the roadmap's coded check and opens wave B by default. Nothing in Gmail is changed, labelled, drafted or sent, and the agent cannot browse, run code or message anyone but its owner.
example: Tony texts: 'Did the dentist confirm Thursday?' and gets the sender, the date and one line of gist from his own inbox. Trigger, 07:00, text to Tony: 'Mail that needs you: the plumber asks you to confirm Thursday's visit by tomorrow; the car insurance renewal is due on 20 October. Nothing else needs a reply.'
how:
Connector: nothing new is written. Chosen by Tony on 11 Oct: gog's own MCP server (`gog mcp`, the CLI behind the bundled gog skill), run on the Mac mini with a token limited to Gmail read-only. Not chosen: Google's hosted Gmail MCP server at `https://gmailmcp.googleapis.com/mcp/v1` (Streamable HTTP with OAuth, which OpenClaw can connect to with `auth: "oauth"` and `openclaw mcp login`); it is in Developer Preview, its setup lists `gmail.compose` next to `gmail.readonly`, and its tools include drafts and labels, so it is the wider grant and would need a tool filter. Either route needs a Google Cloud project with an OAuth client, set up once. Agent (G015): one `

-mail` entry per adult with `profile: "minimal"`, an explicit `

-gmail__*` allow plus the `tools.sandbox.tools` gate, web, fs, runtime and browser denied, memory search off; checked with `openclaw sandbox explain --agent`. Tool (F047): `gog mcp` as a host-side stdio entry under `mcp.servers`, narrowed with `--allow-tool` to the Gmail read tools (its default also registers Drive, Docs, Sheets and Calendar reads); one token per adult from `gog auth add` with `--services` limited to Gmail and `--gmail-scope readonly`. Lookup: `

-main` spawns `

-mail` through `subagents.allowAgents`. Digest (F016): an isolated 07:00 job on `

-mail` with `--tools "

-gmail__*,llm-task"`, announced to the owner only; health senders by subject line only. Tax forms (F061): a Saturday job, January to April, on the same agent.
caveats: The read-only grant (`gmail.readonly`) lets the connector read every message in the account. Keeping a job to school senders is that job's fixed search, plus a hook check still to be built; it is not a limit of the token.
Both connectors need the same one-time Google setup: a Google Cloud project, an OAuth client and each parent's approval on the consent screen. A hosted connector does not remove that step.

The roadmap's M4 keeps each inbox on a local model and none is installed, so the lookup and the digest both send personal mail to the cloud model, and without Zero Data Retention the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to that text; Tony's direction of 11 Oct is to read Gmail through an existing connector, and he has agreed to apply for Zero Data Retention; until OpenAI approves it the 30-day log applies.

Waiting for a local model is not the safer choice on every count. OpenClaw's security page says not to use older, weaker or smaller model tiers for untrusted inboxes or for agents that hold tools (gateway/security/prompt-injection.md:47). The roadmap's local-model milestone says no local model gets tools that touch untrusted content, while its mail milestone allows the reader one read-only mail tool if the Gmail route is chosen, and the lookup cannot work without that search tool. So the decision trades privacy (mail text stays on the Mac) against resistance to a mail written to mislead (the stronger cloud model).

Google already does much of this where the mail lives: the Gemini app answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest of calendar, to-dos and emails among its scheduled actions, and Gmail's 'AI Inbox' was announced in January 2026, so try those on one parent's account before building; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags come from upstream docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the installed version.
With sandbox mode all, MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob, and the minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly.

A Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the app is published to In production (the consent screen then shows a warning) or each adult signs in again every week; whether both adults' tokens can share one keyring under the happy user is still open.

'Send pinned to owner' applies only when the mail agent runs its own scheduled turn, because a mail agent spawned from `

-main` always loses `message` and `session_status`; that a before_tool_call hook reaches MCP tool calls is implied by the docs but not stated.
'Memory off' is not one switch: memory search has a per-agent override, dreaming is plugin-wide, and the session-exclusion setting only matches hook sessions.

Reply drafts are left out, 'subject line only for health senders' and 'do not open the form' are instructions to the agent and not enforced limits, and the tax-form check only knows that a notice email arrived, so a form that came by post or sits in a portal shows as missing.

The lookup goes one step beyond the roadmap's design, where a mail agent's only output is its scheduled text to the owner: here the answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's notes and may hand a task to the research helper (F019). OpenClaw's security page recommends the first half of this shape (a read-only reader agent summarises untrusted content and passes the summary to the main agent, gateway/security/prompt-injection.md:34) and warns about the second: deny `sessions_spawn` to an agent that handles untrusted content (gateway/security/tool-permissions.md:21), and the parent's agent keeps that tool for the research hand-off, which the roadmap already names as its one remaining leak path. So the lookup needs its own test with a seeded misleading mail, or the card can start with the digest alone.
corrections: The 9 Oct needs list omits the sandbox-layer gate: with sandbox mode 'all', MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130). The minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly either (same file, lines 36 and 41).

'Memory off' is not one switch in the installed docs: memory search has a per-agent override (`agents.entries.*.memory.search`, `enabled`, docs/reference/memory-config.md:31 and :102), dreaming is plugin-wide (docs/concepts/memory.md:275), and `excludeSessions.hookExternalContentSources` only matches hook sessions (docs/reference/memory-config.md:667).

'Send pinned to owner' only applies when the mail agent runs its own scheduled or hook turn: when spawned from `

-main` it always loses `message` and `session_status` (docs/tools/subagents/tool-policy.md:23), so its allow list must not consist of `session_status` alone.
The 9 Oct needs list puts `openclaw models status --agent --probe` in the deploy checks; the installed doc says a direct probe needs the Gateway stopped (docs/cli/models.md:121).

The 9 Oct verifier note says gogcli has no read-only-only Gmail scope. The upstream command reference lists `--gmail-scope full|readonly|send|read-send` and says `--readonly` on `gog auth add` requests read-only OAuth scopes, so a read-only grant can be requested; the catalog's hedge 'if the installed version supports it' can be firmed up, pending a check on the installed binary.

The 9 Oct text treats the `

-gmail` wrapper as new code. Upstream gogcli ships a stdio MCP server (`gog mcp`) that exposes only read tools unless `--allow-write` is passed, so the config entry can run gog directly with an `--allow-tool` list and no wrapper.

The 9 Oct needs list stops at the per-agent allow list. With sandbox mode 'all' (Happy's setting) the installed docs add a second gate: MCP tools are filtered out unless `tools.sandbox.tools` also names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob (docs/gateway/config-tools/tool-policy.md:101 and :130).
unverified: That Google offers no narrower Gmail read scope (per label or per sender) was not re-checked against its scope list in this step.
Google's page for its hosted Gmail MCP server does not say whether personal @gmail.com accounts can use it, and it requires membership of the Workspace Developer Preview Program.
The per-person provider setting that sends store false was verified in M1 and not re-read here.
Whether this OpenAI account has zero retention; without it the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to mail text sent to the model.
Whether personal mail may go to the cloud model under store:false is Tony's open decision; no source settles it.
The promptfoo boundary and injection canaries are in-house tests, not OpenClaw features.
A before_tool_call hook reaching MCP tool calls is implied by the doc ('every tool call in the run', docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md:222), but no sentence naming MCP tools was found.

gog is not installed on this Mac; its flags (`--gmail-scope readonly` and `--services` on `gog auth add`, `--allow-tool` on `gog mcp`) come from the upstream main-branch docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the version Homebrew installs.

Whether both adults' tokens would sit in one keyring under the happy user: upstream says tokens use the platform keyring by default with a file backend for headless hosts; splitting them with a per-adult GOG_HOME is an inference from the paths doc.

That publishing the self-made Google sign-in app to In production, as gog's quickstart describes, keeps a read-only Gmail token alive past seven days on a personal, unverified app was not tested; Google's scope page marks gmail.readonly as a Restricted scope.

Whether Gmail's AI Inbox is available on the parents' accounts in October 2026: Google's January 2026 announcement was read, and later press coverage tying it to paid Google AI plans was seen only in search results.
safety: The mail agent holds private mail and reads untrusted mail text, so it gets no way out of its own: no web, file, code or browser tools, no draft or send tool, and texts only to the mailbox's owner. The digest runs unattended on that same agent. The lookup is the weaker half: its answer returns into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's memory and can hand a task to the research helper, so a mail written to mislead could reach the hand-off that the roadmap names as its one remaining leak path. The relayed answer has to be treated as untrusted (a prompt rule, not an enforced limit), and a seeded-mail test has to show that it cannot make the parent's agent pass anything to research. The other open question is the model: personal mail would go to the cloud model.

sources.title: Configure the Gmail MCP server (Google for Developers)
sources.supports: Google runs a hosted Gmail MCP server over Streamable HTTP with OAuth; it is in the Workspace Developer Preview Program and its setup lists the gmail.readonly and gmail.compose scopes.

sources.title: Connect MCP servers
sources.supports: OpenClaw connects to stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP MCP servers, can expose only some of a server's tools, and signs in to an HTTP server that uses OAuth.

adds: From F050 (IMAP mailbox watch on a personal Gmail (allowlisted senders, per-message reader)): In F047, note that F060 and F061 should run as scheduled sweeps of the read-only Gmail tool limited to named senders, in place of an IMAP watch. Say plainly what is lost: that limit becomes a fixed search query or an in-house check instead of the mail plugin's built-in sender list, and F060's headers-only setting for health senders belonged to the plugin and needs a new answer. The note that the IMAP plugin cannot text a person by itself moves to F051, where the plugin is still used on the dedicated school mailbox.

From F052 ('Did I get an email about X?' lookup and thread summary): Give F047 the example ('did the dentist confirm?' returns sender, date and gist, or a five-line thread timeline) and the hand-off:

-main spawns

-mail through subagents.allowAgents and gets a bounded answer back.

From F045 (More read-only Google data per person: Sheets, Docs, Drive and Contacts): Carry over one source only: the gog quickstart page (https://gogcli.sh/quickstart), which says a Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days. G015's caveat relies on that page but does not list it. The Drive, Docs, Sheets and Contacts lookups themselves are not carried over.

From F060 (Appointment, refill, results and travel-change emails to .ics, reminders and alerts): If the morning mail digest (F016) is built, let its deadline lines mention appointment and travel-change mail, and keep the rule that mail from health senders is summarised from the subject line only. A parent who wants one appointment on the calendar can still send Happy the confirmation and get a calendar-file proposal (F010, F011).

From F061 (Tax document checklist (January to April)): Add a seasonal leg to the mail digest: on Saturdays from January to April the same read-only mail agent searches for arrival notices from the family's own list of expected tax-form senders and texts 'arrived' with the date or 'still missing'. It only knows that a notice email arrived (forms that come by post or sit in a portal show as missing), 'do not open the form' is an instruction and not an enforced limit, and the job is switched off by hand after filing.

history: r1: edited depends_on. Kept as the operator guardrail for the roadmap's M4 rule: one mail agent per inbox with minimal tools and no files, web or runtime; the vendor's restricted-reader pattern is the mechanism. The record had no dependency list, so two are written in: it has no use without the read-only Gmail tool (F047), and the roadmap wanted this agent on a local model, which does not exist yet.
r1: kept; credible mention: IMAP email trigger: verify the security boundary

r1: merged with F047 (same batch). The locked-down per-person mail agent and the read-only Gmail tool that is the only thing it reads are one build with one account grant, so they become one wave C card; drafts, email-to-self and the morning digest stay separate.

r2: edited depends_on, caveats, unverified, safety. Kept: it is the roadmap's M4 rule (one locked-down mail agent per inbox) built on the vendor's restricted-reader pattern, and Google's own assistant offers the same 'find it in my Gmail' lookup. The dependency on the removed drafts item is dropped, and an open question is answered: sign-in tokens from a Google app left in Testing expire after seven days, so the app has to be published.
r2: kept; credible mention: Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help

r3: edited value. Kept: it is the roadmap's M4 rule (one locked-down mail agent per inbox) built on the vendor's restricted-reader pattern, and the morning digest (F016) runs on it. Value drops from 5 to 4: since it was scored, the drafts and appointment-email features that were to share this reader have been removed, and the record now says Gmail and Google's Gemini app already answer 'did I get an email about X?', so what is left is asking from the iMessage thread and carrying the digest.
r3: kept; credible mention: Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help

r3: merged with F016 (same batch). The locked-down per-adult mail agent with its read-only Gmail tool and the 07:00 digest (with its Saturday tax-form check) that runs on that agent are one M4 build behind one open decision, so they become one wave C card; round 1 kept the digest apart while it still carried reply drafts, which have since been removed, and effort rises to L for two medium-sized halves.

r4: edited unverified, safety, caveats, depends_on. Kept, as in round 3: it is the roadmap's morning-mail milestone built on the vendor's restricted mail-reader pattern, Google's own assistant offers the same lookup, and the whole card still waits on Tony's decision about personal mail and the cloud model. Two fixes: the open-questions list no longer says there is no read-only sign-in option (the upstream command reference lists one), and the safety note now says that a lookup's answer returns into the parent's own agent, which can hand tasks to the research helper, so that route needs its own test.
r4: kept; credible mention: Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help

r5: edited caveats. Kept, as in rounds 3 and 4: it is the roadmap's morning-mail milestone built on the vendor's restricted mail-reader pattern, and Google's own assistant offers the same lookup. One thing the earlier rounds did not use is OpenClaw's own security page: it recommends a read-only reader agent that passes a summary to the main agent (the shape of the lookup) and says not to run untrusted inboxes on weaker or smaller models, so Tony's open choice between the cloud model now and a local model later is a trade between privacy and resistance to a misleading mail. Two caveats now say so; the roadmap's own allowance of one read-only mail tool for the reader is stated beside its rule that local models get no tools touching untrusted content.
r5: kept; credible mention: Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help

r6 (Tony's decisions, 11 Oct): Tony: school mail lands in both parents' personal Gmail and Happy should read it through an existing Gmail connector with a token, not a separate mailbox. This card moves to wave B as the connection the school digest (F051) needs; its 07:00 digest and lookup stay as later steps.
r7 (Tony's decisions, 11 Oct (2)): Tony: move the whole-inbox features to wave B, because once the whole inbox is read the school digest is trivial; and use gog as the connector.

r8 (Wave definition, 12 Oct): moved from wave B to wave A. Tony asked on 12 Oct for mail reading to be in wave A; its 07:00 text ships there, and its lookup half opens wave B unless he chooses it over the coded check.
r9 (Wording to match the waves, 12 Oct): Wave wording brought in line with the 12 Oct wave definition: the 07:00 text is in wave A; the lookup opens wave B by default.
